output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger billing adjustments to the back-office Billing Resolution team. Referred billing calls rose from 7% to 54% in the same week FCR dropped. Referred calls resolve at about 33% versus 82% for the rest, and 58% of repeat contacts after a referral asked about status. The April intake refers at the same rate as veteran agents, and veterans' FCR fell by the same amount (75% to 67%). The IVR redesign came two weeks after the drop and the tariff mix shift is small, so both are unlikely causes. I'm fairly confident, around 80–85%. Complaints rising after the drop is only association. Next steps: drop the proposed performance plans for April-intake agents, which would punish the wrong group. Work with Finance on a revised credit authority backed by post-call sampling, and trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. The Finance controller has said they would consider this. Ask MI for the breakdown on the trial teams, since it can be rerun within a day. A full dashboard rebuild isn't needed yet.
